name: OmniBench
intro: OmniBench 是要求同时结合静态图像、音频与文本作答的三模态基准，固定发布含1,142道四选一问答、八类任务与语音/声音事件/音乐三类音频；论文、数据和README在任务数及许可表述上存在需要保留的来源差异。
org: M-A-P, University of Manchester, Queen Mary University of London, 01.AI, HKUST, Nanjing University, Dartmouth College
build_method: 16名标注员编写必须联合依赖图像和音频的四选一问题, 5名质检员交叉复核, LLaVA-1.6-34B进行有限信息可解性检查并迭代修订
metric: 发布计分脚本意图：准确率为正确数/1,142，并单列空问题与三类音频统计；但固定标答经同一解析器仅 711 条映射正确、274 条回退 N/A、157 条误选，脚本在第 12 号样例即断言失败
modality: 图像, 音频, 文本
task_type: 三模态理解, 多项选择问答
eval_feature: 图像与音频联合必要性, 单模态消融, 文本近似模态, 人类音乐家基线
scale: 1,142题（771语音、265声音事件、106音乐），三大类、八类任务；固定Git JSONL 与 HF 训练集名包装均为1,142条
build_method_en: Sixteen annotators author four-option questions that require both image and audio, five inspectors cross-review them, and LLaVA-1.6-34B checks limited-information solvability through iterative revision
eval_feature_en: Joint image-audio necessity, single-modality ablations, textual modality approximations, human musician baseline
intro_en: OmniBench is a tri-modal benchmark that requires jointly using static-image, audio, and text evidence. The fixed release contains 1,142 four-option questions, eight tasks, and speech, sound-event, and music audio; task-count and license wording differ across the paper, data, and README and are preserved as source boundaries.
scale_en: 1,142 questions: 771 speech, 265 sound event, and 106 music; three primary categories and eight task types; both the fixed Git JSONL and train-labelled HF packaging contain 1,142 rows
metric_en: Intended released-scorer formula: accuracy is correct responses divided by 1,142, with empty-question invalids and audio-type breakdowns; on fixed gold answers the parser yields 711 correct indices, 274 N/A, and 157 wrong indices, so calculate_metrics.py asserts at index 12

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18. Primary-source audit fixed the paper to arXiv:2409.15272v6, last revised 2025-12-29; the downloaded PDF SHA-256 is e68151f006ae382ab756c07f9993dbdc420a0335e9928e542d592d4c25663618. The official multimodal-art-projection/OmniBench repository was inspected at immutable commit 1f14e7f49c9a06ff21804d8b5a5c87a116a94361, and the m-a-p/OmniBench Hugging Face dataset was inspected at immutable commit 84dc3923e0f64b3c5926b32d2b08066cf67b3d15. Fixed-file evidence includes Git README.md SHA-256 7ba053f4d3335b0c54ee13d4ad53fad0b1b006e3a6db93b796eab94a795dcb68, dataset/batch-5_1142_20240817.jsonl SHA-256 596c7d0afce4068b2afa8b229f4f0e96e26ee250619fd35dda3f4c2e9d33dfba, inference/answer_parsing.py SHA-256 cb4c714428d32f19cfdce68f6229aef9a5d5b3cd5d997c550d3845450098b3b4, inference/calculate_metrics.py SHA-256 0085ad23821d9ae2257ca789bd782a30b953109a17e4ec768eea0585ff27e5b0, inference/demo_api_call.py SHA-256 7ba74f700a4027667417cccd9a989ab2d9ac468a634814016946f1414e8fc453, and fixed HF README SHA-256 216dd0e61642793515dda2457f033c2ff01b910016fe681f682a51092c934850. Paper section 3 defines the benchmark contract as one static image, one audio clip, and a textual question with four options; the model must reconstruct a shared context and return a textual answer. Although source materials may come from online videos, video is not an input modality in OmniBench, and Appendix B.4 explicitly motivates using a static image plus audio to control modality composition. The task taxonomy has three primary categories and eight concrete task types: current action and activity, story description, plot inference, object identification and description, contextual and environmental questions, identity and relationship, text and symbols, and count and quantity. Construction draws images from online image/video sources, AI generation, or self-prepared assets, and draws audio from online video, sound events, or dialogue recording. Sixteen full-time industry annotators and five quality inspectors with higher-education backgrounds participated. Every item is a four-option MCQ with one intended answer and at least one confusing distractor; annotators reject trivial patterns and require both visual and acoustic evidence. The fixed constraints are at least 480P or 854×480 for images, at most 30 seconds for audio, no more than five occurrences for one speaker, and at most three questions with a similar environmental context. Each item includes an audio transcript or music caption plus separate image and audio rationales. Human quality control cross-inspects every item, records a detailed failure reason, and returns failures for targeted revision. The second quality stage uses LLaVA-1.6-34B under image-plus-text, transcript-plus-text, and text-only conditions, with the text-only condition repeated three times. Acceptance requires the model to reject or answer incorrectly in every limited-information setting, which is the paper's operational test that both modalities are necessary. Failed items loop back for revision; 121 QA pairs (9.58%) are classified as hard to recycle and discarded during iterative quality checking. The paper reports that 868 accepted samples, 76%, required no modification and 21.1% required one or two revision rounds. Final statistics are preserved exactly: 1,142 questions, 771 speech, 265 sound-event, and 106 music items. The fixed Git JSONL was independently counted as 1,142 records with contiguous indices 0 through 1,141; every record has four options and its answer occurs in those options. Its eight task-type counts match the paper table: 251 action/activity, 230 story description, 237 plot inference, 211 object identification/description, 141 contextual/environmental, 32 identity/relationship, 25 text/symbols, and 15 count/quantity. HF commit 84dc3923e0f64b3c5926b32d2b08066cf67b3d15 packages the same benchmark as a single split named train with 1,142 examples; that split label is packaging and not evidence that OmniBench is a training set. Evaluation branches are distinct. The full setting supplies image, audio, and text. Ablations remove image or audio. Textual approximations use image caption plus audio, image plus audio transcript, or caption plus transcript. The paper also averages three musicians for a human-expert baseline. The released prompt family asks the model to answer from the supplied modalities and choose only one of A–D. The fixed parser searches in order for parenthesized letters, plain letters, and dotted letters, and attempts full option-text matching only when the response contains more than five whitespace-delimited tokens. Its multi-candidate paths use a last-match heuristic, but the dotted-letter path reuses the plain-letter lookup; genuine dotted candidates therefore tie at -1 and numpy.argmax selects the first candidate. calculate_metrics.py intends to use N/A as response fallback, treat an empty stored question as invalid, and report correct responses divided by all 1,142 rows with audio-type breakdowns. It also parses every dataset gold answer with the same parser and asserts that the parsed gold is not N/A. A read-only replay over the fixed 1,142-row JSONL yields only 711 correct gold option indices, 274 N/A results, and 157 wrong indices; the first N/A is fixed-data index 12, so the released scorer asserts before producing its intended report. The four-choice random baseline is 25%, but the displayed correct-over-1,142 report is code intent rather than a verified runnable result on the fixed release. Source drift is preserved rather than silently normalized. The fixed README says seven task types, while paper Table 1 and the fixed JSONL both show eight. The fixed demo_api_call.py defaults to batch-5_1142_20240817.xlsx, which is absent from the fixed Git tree, reads it with pandas.read_excel, and expects option plus correct answer fields; the released JSONL and HF package instead expose options plus answer, so the data-to-demo handoff is not directly compatible. The demo then appends one JSON object per line, producing JSONL, while calculate_metrics.py reads the inference file with json.load as a single JSON value, so the demo-to-metric handoff is also not directly compatible without conversion. The diagram marks this released-code boundary without treating the implementation defect as a paper method. License metadata is also inconsistent: the paper's ethics discussion says the dataset will use CC-BY-NC and later describes a restricted noncommercial license, while the checklist's asset answer says the benchmark is MIT; the fixed Git tree has no LICENSE file and the fixed HF card has no license field. Accordingly the page reports public availability but does not invent a definitive license. The paper limitation prose also says about 1,000 manually curated examples, but exact paper tables and both fixed releases say 1,142; the exact artifacts control the displayed scale. No task, curation gate, metric, parser, or openness detail was inferred beyond these fixed paper, Git, and HF sources. Formal publication evidence [site-a12a-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2885×861 (English) and 2885×861 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2883×859 and 2883×859. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
